pageCache.pageTitle: How to support your child if they are being bullied - Latest News - Grove Academy
pageCache.text:
Latest News
How to support your child if they are being bullied
We understand that school is an important place for children to develop emotional and socially. This doesn’t happen without mistakes and incidents, and these are all part of the children’s learning and development.
Unfortunately, in all schools, bullying sometimes occurs and it is important it is addressed and that our students know what to do if it happens to them. Unkindness is different to bullying, however repeated incidents of unkind behaviour can become bullying.
For information about how we deal with bullying and unkind behaviour and how you can support your children, read this document.
If your child is being bullied and they do not follow the ways to report it in school, please contact the school and report it for them. You can do this by emailing: safeguarding@groveacademy.co.uk

This month, students have been demonstrating their literary prowess by drafting a novel! Students were provided with a brief to write the first chapter of a novel that engages the senses and introduces the reader to characters with depth.

It’s no surprise to us that we have so many creative and talented students at Grove Academy. We are so impressed with the standard and quality of novel writing and very proud of our students for participating in National Novel Writing Month and publishing their work.

pageCache.text:
Latest News
Grove Academy's Winter Fayre: A Snowy Spectacle of Joy! ❄️
The winter magic descended upon Grove Academy School in Slough, transforming our campus into a festive wonderland! Our recent Winter Fayre was nothing short of a triumph, leaving students, parents, and staff brimming with holiday cheer.
Student-Run Markets:
Marvel at the extraordinary talents of our students as they transformed our hallways into a bustling marketplace! From delectable treats to unique wonders, the spirit of entrepreneurship was alive as our students set up their own stores, creating a vibrant and engaging atmosphere at Grove Academy's Winter Fayre!
Santa's Enchanted Grotto:
The highlight of the day was the enchanting visit to Santa's Grotto! Excitement filled the air as students had the chance to share their wishes with the man in red and receive a special treat in return. It truly was a magical moment for everyone involved.
Games Galore with Teachers:
Laughter and camaraderie echoed through the school as students engaged in friendly games with our amazing teachers. From classic board games to interactive challenges, the joy of playful competition brought our school community even closer together.
Donkey Delight:
Our furry friends added an extra touch of charm to the festivities! Students had the opportunity to pet and interact with adorable donkeys, creating heartwarming memories that will last a lifetime.
Carols in the Snow:
Yes, you read that right—carols in the snow! We brought the winter magic to life with a snowy serenade. Students and staff joined together to sing heartwarming carols, creating a picturesque scene that warmed even the chilliest of days.
Embracing the Cold:
Despite the winter chill, spirits remained high, and the cold was forgotten in the glow of joyful moments. The warmth of community and the festive atmosphere made it a day to remember.
A huge thank you to everyone who contributed to the success of Grove Academy's Winter Fayre! Your enthusiasm and participation turned a cold day into a heartwarming celebration. Let's carry this festive spirit into the holiday season and beyond. Happy holidays, Grove Academy!

pageCache.pageTitle: World Book Day 2025 - Latest News - Grove Academy
pageCache.text:
Latest News
World Book Day 2025
World Book Day was celebrated throughout Grove Academy.
Early Years enjoyed traditional stories, such as Goldilocks and The Three Bears, and practiced their drawing skills by creating the characters themselves.
The theme for primary was ‘Cosy up with a book’ – the students came in their pyjamas and really enjoyed bringing their own books and reading stories together as a class.
Each class in secondary were read one part of a story at the beginning of each lesson until they completed all 5 parts of the story at the end of the day. They were eager to find out what was going to happen each period! The students also got involved with reading new books in the library and completing word searches involving famous authors.
The teachers did a fantastic job of dressing up in their own costumes, which the students loved!

pageCache.pageTitle: Ramadan Iftar Event 2025 - Latest News - Grove Academy
pageCache.text:
Latest News
Ramadan Iftar Event 2025
We welcomed our local community into Grove Academy for our Ramadan Iftar event on Friday 7th March.
Our Iftar began with wonderful performances from our students: Ayaan, Wasif, Muskan, and Manahil. Fast was broken with dates, spring rolls and samosas. The main meal was enjoyed by all guests, consisting of chicken curry, vegetable curry, raita and naan. Thank you to our wonderful kitchen team for preparing the food, led by Mr Skyes.
We were pleased to welcome Mr Tan Dhesi MP to our Iftar event. Mr Dhesi joined our local community to dinner.
Thank you to all of the families that attended the event and made it special.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wellbeing During Exam Season - Latest News - Grove Academy
pageCache.text:
Latest News
Wellbeing During Exam Season
With exams fast approaching it is normal for students to feel a little worried and nervous about them. The pressure of exams can cause some children to feel anxious which can affect sleeping and eating habits.
Support is always available at school. Please ensure students speak to their class teacher, form tutor or any member of staff they trust and feel comfortable with.
How you can help your child study
Make sure your child has somewhere comfortable to study. Ask them how you can support them with their revision.
Help them come up with practical ideas that will help them revise, such as drawing up a revision schedule or getting hold of past papers for practice.
To motivate your child, encourage them to think about their goals in life and see how their revision and exams are related to them. Remind your child that it’s normal to feel anxious. Nervousness is a natural reaction to exams. The key is to put these nerves to positive use.
Encourage them to think about what they know and the time they’ve already put into studying to help them feel more confident.
Exercise can help boost energy levels, clear the mind and relieve stress. It does not matter what it is – walking, cycling, swimming, football and dancing are all effective.
A balanced diet is vital for your child’s health and can help them feel well during exam periods.
Good sleep improves thinking and concentration. Most teenagers need about 8 hours sleep a night. Cramming all night before an exam is usually a bad idea.
Sleep will benefit your child far more than a few hours of panicky last-minute study.
To support your child at home, it can be helpful to look out for some signs of stress, these can include:
• headaches and stomach pains
• loss of interest in food or eating more than normal
• not enjoying activities they previously enjoyed
• being negative and having a low mood
• feeling hopeless about the future
Encourage your child to talk to a member of school staff who they feel is supportive. If you think your child is not coping, it may also be helpful for you to talk to their teachers.
If you have any questions or feel that you or your child require further support, reach out the Head of Year via office@groveacademy.co.uk.

pageCache.pageTitle: Sky Up Trip - Latest News - Grove Academy
pageCache.text:
Latest News
Sky Up Trip
Year 11 students visited the Sky Campus in London for a careers trip and had a tremendously enjoyable time.
While at the Sky Campus, the students received a tour of the building, seeing some of the exciting features Sky has to offer as a broadcasting giant. They had the opportunity to see Sky Sports being recorded live and get an extremely close view of the daytime presenters.
The group then created a news report on climate change. The students each took on a role to create a 5 min video. Between them, students adopted roles as the producer, script writer, director, camera operator, journalist and actors. Working together in Sky’s state of the art studio, the students produced a high-quality broadcast whilst presenting and conducting themselves professionally both in front of and behind the camera.

pageCache.pageTitle: Proposal to change the length of the school day - Latest News - Grove Academy
pageCache.text:
Latest News
Proposal to change the length of the school day
I am writing to inform you of a proposed change to the structure of the school day at Grove Academy in line with other SEBMAT settings. Leaders are proposing to adjust the timings of the school day on a Friday. Students will start school at the normal time but will end the school day as follows:
- The end of the school day on a Friday will be 2.30pm for students in Key Stage 3
- The end of the school day on a Friday will be 2.35pm for students in Key Stage 4
- The end of the school day on a Friday will be 2.40pm for students in EYFS/Key Stage 1
- The end of the school day on a Friday will be 2.50pm for students in Key Stage 2
The school day will remain as current from Monday to Thursday each week. Should the changes be agreed, the new system will begin from –
Monday 24th February 2025 for students in Key Stage 3 and Key Stage 4
Tuesday 22nd April 2025 for students in EYFS, Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2
We hope that this will allow parents and carers sufficient time to make any adjustments to end of day collection. The school will still offer wrap around care at the current cost to primary students.
We believe that these changes will be beneficial to the school community and will have a positive effect on our children’s education. This time will be used by staff for collaborative precision planning to deliver high quality teaching and learning.
I appreciate that these changes may affect you in terms of childcare or working arrangements, and you may have questions related to your child’s education. For this reason, I would like to invite you to please share any feedback that you have by sending it to office@groveacademy.co.uk before midday on Thursday 13th February 2025.
We will share summary feedback on Friday 14th February 2025 via the school website.
